question.problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{8}{x-2y+3z}?$
question.worked_solution:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \frac{8}{x-2y+3z} & =c \\ 8 & =c(x-2y+3z) \\ cx-2cy+3cz-8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $f(x,y,z)$ can't be zero. Therefore, we get a family of planes:

$$
cx-2cy+3cz-8=0,\,c\in (-\infty ,0)\cup (0,\infty ).
$$

choices.value: A family of surfaces given by $z=\frac{8}{3(x-2y)}$
A family of surfaces given by $z=\frac{8}{x-2y+3}$

responses.value: A family of surfaces given by $z=\frac{8}{3(x-2y)}$
